item.title: Uniqueness of scalar-flat ALE K\"ahler metrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.03736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study uniqueness of scalar-flat K\"ahler metrics in a fixed K\"ahler class on an asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) K\"ahler manifold, assuming only differentiated $o(1)$ decay to a fixed Euclidean metric on the end. In complex dimension $n\geq2$, under suitable polynomial decay of the reference metric, we prove that the relative Mabuchi functional is finite, continuous, and convex along weak geodesics whose endpoint potentials satisfy $u=O(r^{-\gamma})$, $\gamma>2n-4$, together with the corresponding derivative estimates. Combining this convexity with the analysis of the Lichnerowicz operator in weighted spaces, we obtain uniqueness by a perturbation argument. Decay improvement and comparison of the asymptotic charts produce a global potential with the required decay for the difference of the two cohomologous scalar-flat K\"ahler forms. The argument also extends to asymptotically conical K\"ahler metrics approaching a fixed Ricci-flat K\"ahler cone under prescribed decay assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Qi Yao

item.title: Pure Spinor Factorization of Belinski-Zakharov Solitons and Regular Gravitational Instantons
item.description: arXiv:2611.03750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Belinski-Zakharov soliton construction factorizes into signed Pfaffian tau-functions, revealing a pure-spinor description of the metric and its regularity conditions. We derive analytic restrictions on the integral rod data, prove uniqueness for the asymptotically flat balance problem at fixed rod structure and periods, and give a conditional criterion for global existence. Combining these results with exhaustive enumeration of the admissible data and rigorous existence certificates, we construct a catalogue of regular asymptotically flat solutions representing 356 rod-word classes through twelve turning points, and 52 isolated regular asymptotically locally flat solutions through eight turning points. Analytic positivity and smooth-completion results establish regularity beyond the finite numerical solve. Based on this catalogue, we investigate two organizations of the solution space: generalized rank-two root systems and compositions of simpler endpoint geometries. The endpoint composition rules reproduce exactly all retained asymptotically flat words through twelve turning points.
item.dc:creator: Steffen Aksteiner

item.title: Conjugate radius and parabolicity along the Ricci flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.03823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the behaviour of the conjugate radius under the Ricci flow on complete noncompact manifolds. We show that if $(M^n,g(t))_{t\in[0,T]}$ is a complete Ricci flow with nonnegative scalar curvature at $t=0$, the initial metric is parabolic and not Ricci-flat, and the Einstein tensor $\mathrm{Ric}-\tfrac12 Rg$ is bounded above, then parabolicity is preserved along the flow and the conjugate radius of $g(t)$ is finite for every $t\in(0,T]$. As an application, we prove that a complete noncompact gradient shrinking Ricci soliton whose volume growth is subquadratic, in the sense that $\liminf_{r\to\infty}\Vol(B(p,r))/r^2=0$, has finite conjugate radius.
item.dc:creator: Chandan Kumar Mondal

item.title: Biharmonic submanifolds in nonpositive space forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.04159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that there are no proper biharmonic submanifolds with parallel normalized mean curvature vector field in a nonpositive space form, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. We also prove that every biharmonic surface with flat normal bundle in a four-dimensional nonpositive space form is minimal. These results provide substantial support for Chen's conjecture and the generalized Chen's conjecture for hyperbolic space in higher codimensions.
item.dc:creator: Yu Fu, Min-chun Hong, Dan Yang

item.title: A note on the BRST-BV Formalism Explanation of Deformation Quantization and Algebraic Index Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.04258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we begin with considering the simple one-dimensional field theory describing a single free particle on manifold, and apply the BRST formalism and BV quantization to this model following the standard procedures in physics. Through calculations that, while not fully rigorous, have a more transparent physical interpretation, then subsequent geometric identifications, we recover the deformation quantization and algebraic index theorem on symplectic manifold. This note thus elucidates the physical origins and mechanisms of these mathematical results.
item.dc:creator: Lihao Zhao

item.title: Strong $G_2$-structures with torsion: a survey and new examples
item.description: arXiv:2611.04460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article has two main parts. The first consists of a brief survey of $G_2$-structures with torsion, namely $G_2$-structures admitting a $G_2$-connection with totally skew-symmetric torsion. We focus primarily on the strong condition that the associated torsion $3$-form is closed. We review their basic properties and their connections with the heterotic $G_2$ system, generalized geometry, and six-dimensional geometry. In the second part, we construct two complete cohomogeneity-one strong $G_2T$-structures on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3\times S^3$ with non-zero closed and co-closed characteristic torsion, and non-vanishing characteristic Ricci tensor. Both have an asymptotically cylindrical end; at the other end, the first is asymptotically conical (AC), with a torsion-free $G_2$ cone as its asymptotic model, while the second is asymptotically locally conical (ALC), with a constant-length circle bundle over a Calabi--Yau cone as its asymptotic model. We investigate the induced $SU(3)$-structures on their circle quotients and show that they are globally conformally almost K\"ahler and globally conformally K\"ahler, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, these provide the first complete strong $G_2T$-structures whose underlying metrics are not locally Riemannian products.
item.dc:creator: Anna Fino, Udhav Fowdar

item.title: Prescribed combinatorial curvature beyond positivity for spherical vertex scalings on the sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.04478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(S,V)$ be a marked 2-sphere with $|V|\ge3$, and fix a spherical discrete conformal class. Izmestiev-Prosanov-Wu proved existence and uniqueness for positive prescribed combinatorial curvature in the spherical discrete conformal class on $(S,V)$. In this paper, we identify a region of prescribed combinatorial curvature vectors, allowing some negative components, for which existence still holds.
item.dc:creator: Chen Liu, Xu Xu

item.title: Unbounded total mean curvature with prescribed boundary metric
item.description: arXiv:2611.04762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: B\"ar has shown that a fixed boundary metric and a scalar-curvature lower bound do not generally bound total mean curvature from above. We extend this unboundedness to every smooth compact connected manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with nonempty boundary and every prescribed boundary metric, using scalar-flat metrics. While B\"ar's examples use warped products, our construction uses a nonzero cubic variation of total mean curvature near a flat product, followed by localization and conformal correction. We also construct arbitrarily $C^k$-small perturbations of the flat torical half-cylinder with nonnegative scalar curvature, unchanged boundary metric, an exact product end, and positive total boundary mean curvature.
item.dc:creator: Zhixin Wang

item.title: Hidden Symmetries of the Kepler Problem and Jacobi's Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.04791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a geometric derivation of the hidden symmetries of the Kepler problem, combining a duality for central-force systems, obtained by interchanging positions and velocities, with a generalized form of Jacobi's theorem. Applied to the dual Kepler problem, this theorem identifies Kepler hodographs of prescribed energy with geodesics of a metric of constant curvature. After adjoining one point at infinity, the resulting geometry is complete. Its Killing vector fields induce a finite-dimensional Lie algebra of infinitesimal symmetries on the corresponding energy hypersurface. The distinguished point at infinity determines a canonical decomposition of the Killing algebra into two vector subspaces, whose associated Noether invariants recover angular momentum and the Runge-Lenz vector.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Moreno D\'iaz, Juan B. Sancho de Salas

item.title: Pseudo-Einstein Structures on Links of Isolated Singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.04851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Jack Lee's conjecture that, for a compact strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold $M$, the condition $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{R})$ implies the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. For links of isolated singularities, we construct counterexamples in every odd dimension at least three, with $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{Z})$ and $b_1(M)=0$. For isolated algebraic singularities of log canonical type and complex dimension at least three, we prove that the real Chern class condition is equivalent to $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartierness of the canonical divisor, log canonicity, and the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. Finally, we construct a Du Bois threefold singularity whose link satisfies the real Chern class condition but admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. The initial versions of the proofs were generated with AI assistance and were subsequently revised and verified by the authors.
item.dc:creator: Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, Shuya Matsumoto, Yuya Takeuchi

item.title: A remark on the compactness of manifolds with non-negative Ricci curvature and uniformly convex boundary
item.description: arXiv:2611.04866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Yan-Zhu (arXiv:2605.31477) showed the compactness of complete Riemannian manifolds with non-negative Ricci curvature and uniformly convex boundary. In this paper, we give an alternative proof of this compactness theorem.
item.dc:creator: Yasuaki Fujitani

item.title: Fibrewise Real-Analytic Landsberg Metrics in Dimension at Least Four Are Berwald
item.description: arXiv:2611.05067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge4$, and let $F$ be a smooth, strongly convex Landsberg metric, regular on the entire slit tangent bundle. We prove that $F$ is Berwald if, at each fixed base point, the Minkowski norm is real-analytic on the entire slit tangent space. The proof rests on two analytic rigidity theorems for a single Minkowski space. The first asserts that, in dimension at least $3$, a real-analytic Minkowski norm whose Hessian metric is flat is induced by an inner product. The second asserts that, in dimension at least $4$, the Hessian metric of a real-analytic Minkowski norm is flat if the entire indicatrix carries a nonzero smooth symmetric quartic form satisfying a twisted Codazzi equation. The quartic form need not be real-analytic, and the second theorem is proved independently of the first. Applying these results to the angular Berwald quartic form shows that the metric is Riemannian on the open set of base points on whose fibres the Berwald curvature is not identically zero. Since every Riemannian metric is Berwald, this set must be empty. No analytic structure, compactness or completeness of the base manifold is assumed, and the metric need not be reversible.
item.dc:creator: Ming Li, Kefeng Liu

item.title: A Generalized Lai--Wei Construction and New Families of Area-Minimizing Hypercones
item.description: arXiv:2611.05149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Our results are twofold. Inspired by recent work on weighted spheres, we extend the Lai--Wei construction from one to several independent isoparametric inputs, replacing its profile curve by a hypersurface profile to generate minimal hypersurfaces in spheres. Using a curvature criterion, we obtain new infinite families of area-minimizing hypercones from the original construction and its extensions.
item.dc:creator: Yongsheng Zhang

item.title: A note on cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics on closed 4-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.05288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: K. Broder recently classified the closed Einstein 4-manifolds whose isometry groups have dimension at least three. The proof reduces the problem to the study of cohomogeneity-one Einstein metrics invariant under $SU(2)$, however a few cases are not treated. We reconcile the missing cases using Broder's techniques with minimal modifications.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Donovan

item.title: Diastolic inequalities for the distance function min-max width of spheres
item.description: arXiv:2611.05315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we investigate inequalities involving the min-max width associated to the distance function and the area of two-dimensional Riemannian spheres. This geometric invariant naturally arises as min-max methods are applied for the distance function defined on the space of pairs of points. Our methods involve careful constructions of sweepouts that can be performed under the hypothesis that the Riemannian sphere does not contain stable closed geodesics. Improved bounds are obtained under further geometric assumptions (positive curvature, pinching condition, and antipodal symmetry). In the cases of a pinching condition or antipodal symmetry, our inequalities are optimal.
item.dc:creator: Rafael Montezuma, Idalina Ribeiro

item.title: Toric gravitational instantons with four fixed points
item.description: arXiv:2611.05333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the simply connected toric gravitational instantons whose torus action has four fixed points. They are the hyperk\"ahler multi-Eguchi--Hanson and multi-Taub--NUT metrics with four collinear centres, the asymptotically flat instantons on Li and Sun's manifold $X_3$, up to scale one for each twist at infinity in $(0,1)$ for a fixed orientation of the torus, and, up to scale, a single further instanton with an ALF end, which is not hyperk\"ahler. The last two are Hermitian for neither orientation. In particular, the toric asymptotically flat instanton on $X_3$ with a given twist is unique up to scale, as conjectured by Li and Sun. The proof combines the solitonic form of Geroch's conjecture, which turns smoothness into polynomial equations for the soliton data, with a convexity principle adapted from Aksteiner. At a fixed asymptotic parameter, the cone errors of the conical metrics with a given rod structure are the gradient of a strictly convex function of the rod lengths, and the strict convexity gives uniqueness. Existence follows from an explicit solution for the ALF end and, for the AF ends, from Li and Sun's existence theorem. We also outline how a chart of Aksteiner identifies these AF instantons with those found by Teo.
item.dc:creator: Lars Andersson, Mattias Dahl, Gustav Nilsson

item.title: New type of bubbling solutions to a critical fractional Schr\"{o}dinger equation with double potentials
item.description: arXiv:2410.05271v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the following critical fractional Schr\"odinger equation: \begin{equation} (-\Delta)^s u+V(|y'|,y'')u=K(|y'|,y'')u^{\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}},\quad u>0,\quad y =(y',y'') \in \mathbb{R}^3\times\mathbb{R}^{n-3}, \qquad(0.1)\end{equation} where $n\geq 3$, $s\in(0,1)$, $V(|y'|,y'')$ and $K(|y'|,y'')$ are two bounded nonnegative potential functions. Under the conditions that $K(r,y'')$ has a stable critical point $(r_0,y_0'')$ with $r_0>0$, $K(r_0,y_0'')>0$ and $V(r_0,y_0'')>0$, we prove that equation (0.1) has a new type of infinitely many solutions that concentrate at points lying on the top and the bottom of a cylinder. In particular, the bubble solutions can concentrate at a pair of symmetric points with respect to the origin. Our proofs make use of a modified finite-dimensional reduction method and local Pohozaev identities.
item.dc:creator: Ting Li, Zhongwei Tang, Heming Wang, Xiaojing Zhang

item.title: Learning Directional Randers Geometry for Latent-Space Exploration
item.description: arXiv:2611.03675v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep neural networks extract powerful latent representations from images, enabling fast and efficient downstream analysis. However, these latent spaces lack explicit geometric structure, leading to possibly poor interpolation fidelity and misleading extrapolation. Latent interpolation techniques assume symmetric transition costs which are often not the case for real world data. Their symmetric nature cannot capture directional processes, such as disease progression, where certain transitions are impossible (e.g. tumor growth dynamics or cognitive improvement in Alzheimer's disease). Although Riemannian metrics extend Euclidean geometry by incorporating curvature, they remain symmetric. We show that understanding asymmetry and not curvature alone directly addresses these problems. To do so we propose a new Finsler-Randers metric learning framework. It incorporates direction-dependent distances, thus enabling the computation of trajectories respecting monotonic sequential constraints. We demonstrate its potential for interpolation and extrapolation on controlled cross-sectional datasets.
item.dc:creator: Th\'eau Blanchard (HeKA | U1346, GE Healthcare), St\'ephanie Allassonni\`ere (CMAP)

item.title: Overdetermined boundary problems for maximal graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.04132v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study overdetermined boundary problems for the maximal surface equation with zero Dirichlet data and constant nonzero Neumann data . For the exterior of a bounded domain with connected boundary in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq2$, we prove that such domain must be the complement of a ball and the solution is radial. In dimension two, we also show that a positive solution on a domain bounded by a properly embedded noncompact connected curve forces the domain to be a half-plane and the solution to be affine. The proofs combine the divergence structure of the equation with the induced geometry of maximal graphs.
item.dc:creator: Mijia Lai

item.title: Feynman Propagators on Exponentially Decaying Perturbations of Stationary Spacetimes with Compact Cauchy Surface
item.description: arXiv:2611.04133v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we construct Feynman propagators on exponentially decaying perturbations of stationary spacetime with compact Cauchy surface. The propagators are defined as parametrices of the wave operator on exponentially weighted Sobolev spaces defined by complex contours $\Gamma$. We then apply this theory to the computation of indexes of Dirac operators using a continuous Wick-like rotation to relate it to the Riemannian case.
item.dc:creator: Selim Amar

item.title: Exotic Dehn twists on sums of 4-manifolds, nuclei, and exotic structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.04541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For closed 4-manifolds $X_1, X_2$, we give a sufficient condition, in terms of the Seiberg-Witten invariants of $X_i$, for the Dehn twist on $X_1\#X_2$ along the neck to be smoothly nontrivial. This provides a broad generalization of the result of Kronheimer-Mrowka for $K3\#K3$. We also show that the boundary Dehn twists on the punctured connected sums of many pairs of elliptic surfaces are smoothly nontrivial. We also detect new examples of exotic Dehn twists along Seifert fibered 3-manifolds in elliptic surfaces. As a consequence, we exhibit a new phenomenon in which "exotic diffeomorphisms detect exotic smooth structures on 4-manifolds": the triviality of the boundary Dehn twist characterizes the standard nucleus $N(n)$ among the nuclei $N(n)_{p,q}$ homeomorphic to it, provided that $n\equiv0 \bmod 4$. These results are proved by computing the families Bauer-Furuta invariant for a new framing of the families Dirac index.
item.dc:creator: Hokuto Konno

item.title: Curvature Estimates and Prescribed Curvature Problems for Sum Hessian Equations on Star-Shaped Hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.05032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a closed star-shaped hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ and let $\eta=Hg-h$ be the first Newton transformation of its second fundamental form. For a fixed constant $\alpha>0$ and $2\le k\le n-1$, we study the prescribed sum Hessian curvature equation \[ \sigma_k(\lambda(\eta))+\alpha\sigma_{k-1}(\lambda(\eta))=f(X,\nu). \] Under the natural admissibility condition \[ \lambda(\eta)\in\Gamma_{k-1}\cap \{\lambda:\sigma_k(\lambda)+\alpha\sigma_{k-1}(\lambda)>0\}, \] we establish a global curvature estimate for closed star-shaped solutions with a general positive right-hand side depending on the position vector and the unit normal. A key point is that the sum Hessian operator is nonhomogeneous; the resulting lower-order term in the maximum-principle calculation is controlled by a partial curvature estimate. We also use the augmented-variable identity \[ \sigma_k(\lambda)+\alpha\sigma_{k-1}(\lambda) =\sigma_k(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n,\alpha) \] to recover the relevant ellipticity and concavity properties. As an application of the a priori estimates, we prove existence and uniqueness for the corresponding prescribed curvature problem under suitable spherical barrier and radial monotonicity assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Dongjing Ma, Peihe Wang, Hua Zhu

item.title: Poisson transforms, the BGG complex, and discrete series representations of SU(n+1,1)
item.description: arXiv:2402.08262v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The aim of this article is to construct specific Poisson transforms mapping differential forms on the sphere $S^{2n+1}$ endowed with its natural CR structure to forms on complex hyperbolic space. These transforms have co-closed harmonic values, descend to the BGG (Rumin) complex, and intertwine the differential operators in that complex with the exterior derivative. Passing to the Poincar\'e ball model, we analyze boundary asymptotics, proving that the values of our transforms admit a continuous extension to the boundary in degrees $\leq n$. Finally, we show that composing the exterior derivative with the transform in degree $n$, one obtains an isomorphism between the kernel of the Rumin operator in degree $n$ and a dense subspace of the $L^2$-harmonic forms on complex hyperbolic space. This provides a realization of the disc rete series representations of $SU(n+1,1)$ with trivial infinitesimal character in spaces of differential forms on the compact manifold $S^{2n+1}$. These developments are motivated by a program of the third author to prove some instances of the Baum-Connes conjecture. The first part of the article is valid in a much more general setting, in particular, it is relevant for cases in which the conjecture is still open.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Cap, Christoph Harrach, Pierre Julg

item.title: The min-max width of spheres associated to the distance function
item.description: arXiv:2503.12477v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: What one obtains when the min-max methods for the distance function are applied on the space of pairs of points of a Riemannian two-sphere? This question is studied in details in the present article. We show that the associated min-max width do not always coincide with half of the length of a simple closed geodesic which is the union of two minimizing geodesics with the same endpoints. Therefore, it is a new geometric invariant. We study the structure of the set of minimizing geodesics joining a pair of points realizing the width, and relationships between this invariant and the diameter. The extrinsic case of an embedded Riemannian sphere is also considered.
item.dc:creator: Rafael Montezuma, Idalina Ribeiro

item.title: On the $\mathcal{D}^+_J$ operator on higher-dimensional almost K\"{a}hler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2503.14101v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce $\mathcal{D}^+_J$, a generalization of $\partial\bar{\partial}$ operator on higher dimensional almost K\"{a}hler manifolds. Using the $\mathcal{D}^+_J$ operator, we investigate the $\bar{\partial}$-problem in almost K\"{a}hler geometry and explore the generalized Monge-Amp\`{e}re equation on almost K\"{a}hler manifolds. We establish uniqueness up to an additive constant. We also prove a local existence theorem for this equation on almost K\"{a}hler four-manifold. At last, we find an elliptical system for $\mathcal{D}^+_J$ operator. As an application, we reorganize the result of Tosatti-Weinkove-Yau in \cite{TWY}.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Tan, Hongyu Wang, Ken Wang, Zuyi Zhang

item.title: Verifying spiral minimal product structure through the Takahashi Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2511.12189v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We verify the spiral minimal product structure through the Takahashi Theorem with full computational details which were omitted in [LZ].
item.dc:creator: Yongsheng Zhang

item.title: The 2-systole on compact K\"ahler surfaces with positive scalar curvature
item.description: arXiv:2601.02901v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the 2-systole on compact K\"ahler surfaces of positive scalar curvature. For any such surface $(X,\omega)$, we prove the sharp estimate $\min_X S(\omega)\cdot\operatorname{sys}_2(\omega)\le12\pi$, with equality if and only if $X=\mathbb P^2$ and $\omega$ is the Fubini--Study metric. Using the classification of positive scalar curvature K\"ahler surfaces, we determine the optimal constant in the case that $X$ is rational or non-rational and describe the corresponding rigid models. When $X$ is a non-rational ruled surface, we also give an independent analytic proof, adapting Stern's level set method to the holomorphic fibration in the K\"ahler setting.
item.dc:creator: Zehao Sha

item.title: Sharp quantitative Llarull's theorem and scalar-curvature rigidity with boundary
item.description: arXiv:2601.15043v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a sharp quantitative extension of Llarull's theorem to complete noncompact spin manifolds. Let $\Phi:M\to\mathbf S^m$ be an area-decreasing map of nonzero degree that is locally constant at infinity, and assume that $\operatorname{scal}_{g_M}\geq m(m-1)$ on $\operatorname{supp}(d\Phi)$. If $\lambda_1(M,g_M)=0$, then $\inf_M\operatorname{scal}_{g_M}<0$; if $\lambda_1(M,g_M)>0$, then \[ \inf_M\operatorname{scal}_{g_M}\leq -\frac{4m}{m-1}\lambda_1(M,g_M). \] The coefficient is sharp in every dimension, as shown by an explicit family of warped metrics. We also prove a boundary analogue under the same support-localized scalar-curvature hypothesis, without requiring the strict scalar-curvature positivity condition near the boundary used in Liu--Liu's doubling argument. Applications include a Geroch-type obstruction for connected sums with compact area-enlargeable manifolds and a Ricci-flat splitting theorem for complete metrics with nonnegative scalar curvature and mean-convex boundary.
item.dc:creator: Daoqiang Liu

item.title: Geometry and biological processes
item.description: arXiv:2602.20274v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We suggest a geometric approach to modeling biochemical processes, aiming at those processes that occur in humans with food sensitivities or chemical sensitivities.
item.dc:creator: Tatyana Barron, Sarah Lanthier

item.title: Infinitesimal Hilbertianity for manifolds with Sobolev regular Riemannian metrics through uniform lower capacity bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.03373v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that metric measure spaces arising from $2$-manifolds equipped with Riemannian metrics $g$ such that $g, g^{-1} \in L^\infty_{\rm loc} \cap W^{1,p}_{\rm loc}$ are infinitesimally Hilbertian. Along the way, we establish uniform lower $1$-capacity bounds of several $1$-dimensional subsets of $\R^2$.
item.dc:creator: Vanessa Ryborz

item.title: Ball growth at all scales in universal covers of short metric graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.20088v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a connected metric graph of first Betti number $b\ge 2$, and let $\Gamma_b$ be a trivalent graph of the same Betti number with all edges of unit length. We show that if $\text{length}(\Gamma) \le \lambda\, \text{length}(\Gamma_b)$, then the universal cover of $\Gamma$ contains a vertex around which, at every radius $R\ge 0$, the ball is at least as long as the ball of radius $R$ in the trivalent tree whose edges all have length $3\lambda$. In particular, for $\lambda\le\frac13$, this ball is at least as long as the ball of the same radius in the universal cover of $\Gamma_b$, with no multiplicative loss. This improves an earlier theorem of the author, which gives the weaker lower bound $(1-3\lambda)$ times the ball in the universal cover of $\Gamma_b$, and only for $\lambda\le\frac16$. The proof rests on an elementary comparison principle. Among trees whose vertices have degree at least three and whose edges have length at most $c$, the trivalent tree with all edges of length $c$ has the smallest balls at every radius. As an application, we double the exponential growth rate in the author's earlier uniform lower bound for the area of balls in the universal cover of small-area surfaces of hyperbolic type, from $\ln 2$ to $2\ln 2$, beyond the hyperbolic rate. We also obtain explicit constants in the positive answer to Guth's question for surfaces. Finally, we conjecture the sharp, all-scale version of the minimal volume entropy inequality of Kapovich-Nagnibeda and Lim, and show that it would be optimal.
item.dc:creator: Steve Karam

item.title: Curvature, second variation and Jacobi fields in elastic diffeology
item.description: arXiv:2610.29360v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop curvature theory on Blohmann's elastic diffeological spaces. We introduce curvature-tensorial connections, whose curvature factors uniquely through $T_3M$, and show that this property holds on finite-dimensional manifolds and is preserved on mapping spaces. Using a plotwise commutator identity and the elasticity axioms, we establish the classical curvature symmetries for curvature-tensorial Levi-Civita connections. We define sectional curvature and a curvature form on the algebraic exterior square, and demonstrate an obstruction to the usual Ricci trace construction: on $C^\infty(S^1,S^2)$, the relevant curvature endomorphism extends boundedly to the $L^2$ completion but is not trace class. We express the second variation of the energy by the index form and characterize the null space of the index form by Jacobi fields. Given a geodesic flow, we construct Jacobi fields with prescribed initial data along its flow lines; they are unique when the real line is a curve object for the space. Finally, non-positive sectional curvature excludes conjugate points, while a negative index direction obstructs length minimization; the latter result does not require the curve-object property and applies to mapping spaces such as free loop spaces of complete Riemannian manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Shiobara

item.title: Pure Type-One Generalized Hypercomplex Structures in Dimension Four
item.description: arXiv:2610.35557v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify untwisted generalized hypercomplex structures on four-manifolds whose entire sphere has type one. Their Poisson tensors determine a canonical line field, and their local geometry is described by Gauduchon--Tod coframes. On a closed manifold, the canonical foliation is automatically Riemannian: the non-Riemannian alternative would require a twisting three-form with a nonzero period. Without assuming a circle action, we classify the compact structures into four families, distinguished by their first Betti numbers \(b_1=1,2,3,4\): Berger quotients, flat axis quotients, nontrivial circle bundles over flat three-tori, and constant tori. The underlying manifolds are parallelizable and admit symplectic forms precisely when the intrinsic Gauduchon--Tod invariant vanishes. These results address the four-dimensional untwisted case of the intermediate-type problem posed by Fino and Grantcharov.
item.dc:creator: Guangzhen Ren

item.title: $P=W$ via $\mathcal{H}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2209.05429v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}_2$ be the Lie algebra of polynomial Hamiltonian vector fields on the symplectic plane. Let $X$ be the moduli space of stable Higgs bundles of fixed relatively prime rank and degree, or more generally the moduli space of stable parabolic Higgs bundles of arbitrary rank and degree for a generic stability condition. Let $H^*(X)$ be the cohomology with rational coefficients. Using the operations of cup-product by tautological classes and Hecke correspondences we construct an action of $\mathcal{H}_2$ on $H^*(X)[x,y]$, where $x$ and $y$ are formal variables. We show that the perverse filtration on $H^*(X)$ coincides with the filtration canonically associated to $\mathfrak{sl}_2\subset \mathcal{H}_2$ and deduce the $P=W$ conjecture of de Cataldo-Hausel-Migliorini.
item.dc:creator: Tamas Hausel, Anton Mellit, Alexandre Minets, Olivier Schiffmann

item.title: $L^2$-Betti numbers of Dehn fillings
item.description: arXiv:2412.16090v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We initiate the study of the $L^2$-Betti numbers of group-theoretic Dehn fillings. For a broad class of virtually special groups $G$, we prove that the $L^2$-Betti numbers of sufficiently deep Dehn fillings $\overline{G}$ are equal to those of $G$. As applications, we verify the Singer Conjecture for certain Einstein manifolds, establish a virtual fibering criterion for $\overline{G}$, obtain bounds on deficiency of $\overline{G}$, and provide new examples of hyperbolic groups with exotic subgroups that arise as Dehn fillings of any cusped arithmetic hyperbolic manifold of dimension at least four.
item.dc:creator: Nansen Petrosyan, Bin Sun

item.title: Conformal-DP: A Density-Aware Mechanism for Differential Privacy over Riemannian Manifolds via Conformal Transformation
item.description: arXiv:2504.20941v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Differential Privacy (DP) is being increasingly adopted for non-Euclidean data that lie on complex, high-dimensional manifolds. Existing DP mechanisms for manifold data consider geometric properties when calibrating privacy perturbations, but they largely fail to capture variations in data density within datasets, leading to biased perturbations and suboptimal privacy-utility trade-offs due to heterogeneous data distributions. In this paper, we propose a novel density-aware differential privacy mechanism on Riemannian manifolds, referred to as Conformal-DP, that leverages conformal transformations to calibrate perturbations based on local densities and to induce a density-balanced geometry. We prove that our mechanism satisfies $\epsilon$-differential privacy on any complete Riemannian manifold under mild regularity assumptions. In addition, we derive a closed-form expected geodesic error bound that depends only on the underlying data density ratio and is independent of global curvature. Our empirical results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed Conformal-DP mechanism substantially improves the privacy-utility trade-off in heterogeneous data distribution settings, with worst-case performance comparable to state-of-the-art manifold DP mechanisms that assume uniformly distributed data.
item.dc:creator: Peilin He, Liou Tang, M. Amin Rahimian, James Joshi

item.title: Recovering Geodesic Distances from Noisy Observations
item.description: arXiv:2511.13025v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(M,d,\mu)$ be a nice geodesic probability space (such as a manifold) and $X=\{x_i\}_{i\in [N]} \subset M$ a finite $\mu$-i.i.d. sample. Suppose we observe noisy distance random variables $d'(x_i,x_j)$. When can the true distances be recovered to small additive error? This question has attracted interest in two disparate fields: latent-space graph models and boundary-value inverse problems. We first show that, taking $N \asymp \epsilon^{-2d-2}|\log\epsilon|$ and using runtime $O(N^{2.5+o_d (1)})$, we can recover all distances in $X$ to additive error $O(\epsilon|\log\epsilon|)$ with high probability, assuming $\mathbb{E} d'(x_i, x_j) = F(d(x_i,x_j))$ for an unknown, increasing bilipschitz $F$ and with the $d'(x_i,x_j)$ allowed to be arbitrarily heterogeneous in their distribution as long as they are bounded in subgaussian norm. This generalizes existing work, which required $F$ to be known and made strict assumptions on the distribution of $d'(x_i, x_j)$. Achieving this generalization required a novel ``ruler-building'' procedure to learn $F$. We extend our results to a missing data case where we randomly lose access to noisy distances. Our second result uses ideas from the first to tackle a partial observability case: $X = Y \cup Z$ with $Z$ sampled from $M$ and $Y$ sampled from an observer subset satisfying visibility conditions that model the assumptions made on the boundary in boundary-value inverse problems. In this setting, we recover all pairwise distances in $Z$ to additive error $O(\epsilon)$ with $|Z| \asymp \epsilon^{-2d-2}|\log\epsilon|$, $|Y| \asymp \epsilon^{-\max\{d_\nu,4\}}$ with $d_\nu$ determined by the volume-growth properties of the probability measure on the observer set, and runtime $O(|Z|^3)$. This is, to our knowledge, the first quantitative guarantee for this observer/observed split under noise, which complements existing stability results for boundary data.
item.dc:creator: Charles Fefferman, Jonathan Marty, Kevin Ren

item.title: A Torelli-type theorem for hyperk\"{a}hler quotients
item.description: arXiv:2608.08680v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the moduli space of algebraic asymptotic hyperk\"{a}hler structures on hyperk\"{a}hler quotients arising from a quaternionic vector space $\mathbb{H}^n$. We consider the period map on this moduli space, and prove a Torelli-type theorem (i.e., the bijectivity of the period map) under mild assumptions including the surjectivity of the Kirwan map. This work provides an algebro-geometric generalization of the Torelli-type theorem for ALE gravitational instantons by Kronheimer (1989). In particular, this theorem applies to toric hyperk\"ahler varieties and Nakajima quiver varieties.
item.dc:creator: Ryota Kotani

item.title: Monge's transport problem in synthetic Lorentzian spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2609.17592v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the existence of solutions to the Lorentzian Monge problem on synthetic Lorentzian spacetimes that satisfy the forward timelike measure contraction property $TMCP^+(K,N)$. The cost for this problem is the time separation function $\ell(x,y)$ (the Lorentz distance), which represents the maximum amount a particle can age when traveling from $x$ to $y$. The solution is based on the needle decomposition technique, and amounts to a reduction of the full problem to its one-dimensional counterparts. As an application of needle decomposition, we introduce the blended $TMCP$ condition, and obtain a quantitative refinement of the synthetic Hawking singularity theorem. We additionally prove a timelike nonbranching reversibility theorem for $TCD_p(K,N)$ spacetimes, showing that forward $p$-essentially nonbranching spacetimes are backward $p$-essentially nonbranching.
item.dc:creator: Afiny Akdemir

item.title: Metric foundations of geometry
item.description: arXiv:2609.26410v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A metric space is called all-set-homogeneous if every isometry between two of its subsets extends to an isometry of the whole space. We classify all-set-homogeneous length spaces: besides the classical examples, they include the universal metric trees of finite valence.
item.dc:creator: Nina Lebedeva, Anton Petrunin
